title: When the routine config objects were exposed over the API, two of the eight new viewsets returned every user's rows instead of filtering by owner.

vulnerable_findings.explanation: The `RepsConfigViewSet` and `MaxRepsConfigViewSet` classes return `RepsConfig.objects.all()` and `MaxRepsConfig.objects.all()` respectively in their `get_queryset` methods. findings.explanation: The code uses Django ORM (QuerySet.filter) which utilizes parameterized queries by default. There is no raw SQL execution or string concatenation of user input into SQL statements.

The `RepsConfigViewSet` and `MaxRepsConfigViewSet` classes return `RepsConfig.objects.all()` and `MaxRepsConfig.objects.all()` respectively in their `get_queryset` methods. Unlike other viewsets in the same file (e.g., `WeightConfigViewSet`), these do not filter the queryset by the current user (`self.request.user`). This allows any authenticated user to access, modify, or delete configuration objects belonging to other users (IDOR).
findings.suggested_fix: Modify `get_queryset` in `RepsConfigViewSet` and `MaxRepsConfigViewSet` to filter by the current user, similar to `WeightConfigViewSet`: `return RepsConfig.objects.filter(slot_config__slot__day__routine__user=self.request.user)` and `return MaxRepsConfig.objects.filter(slot_config__slot__day__routine__user=self.request.user)`.
